items.description: One diegetic screen in the world — a screen slab emitted by SdfProgramBuilder whose lit face samples a bound source (or the procedural fallback when unbound). The frame (Origin/Right/ Up + HalfWidth/HalfHeight) is the sampled surface frame and must match the slab's placement; the frame source bakes the geometry translate from it.

index.description: The engine screen-surface index (0..MaxScreenSurfaces−1) this slab declares — the key the source/light providers bind under.

origin.description: The front face's world-space center (the sampled surface origin); the geometry center sits one HalfDepth behind it along the face normal.

right.description: The unit world axis the sampled U increases along (the slab's local +X in world space). Must be orthogonal to Up: the client derives the slab's orientation and UV frame from the pair while the server's collider projects the half-extents onto it, so a skewed pair would render and collide as different solids.

up.description: The unit world axis the sampled V increases against — V = 0 at the top (the slab's local +Y in world space).

halfWidth.description: The face half-width (the slab's local X half-extent).

halfHeight.description: The face half-height (the slab's local Y half-extent).

halfDepth.description: The slab's local Z half-extent (its thickness behind the face).

source.description: The signal the lit face carries.

engageable.description: Whether a player may engage this screen.

engageRadius.description: The world-unit radius a player must be inside to engage (meaningful only when Engageable). Validated finite and non-negative.

autoInsert.description: When set, engaging the screen first boots the selected magazine entry (the "walk over, press the button, the screen lights" gesture), so the interaction is one act rather than an insert then an engage.

engageChannel.description: The world-event channel whose arrival on a body engages this screen, or null (the default) for a route that does not answer gestures. The author chooses this name freely; the engine never special-cases a spelling. Omitted from the wire when null.

cycleChannel.description: Same, for advancing the magazine selector. Omitted from the wire when null.

channels.description: The declared channel names an application onto this screen reaches — a masked-out channel keeps flowing to the source body's own pose (when the own-body application is retained) but never reaches this screen. null (the default) reaches every declared channel. Omitted from the wire when null.

kit.description: The Name whose Pad map an application onto this screen wears, or null for the engine's default pad map. The named kit must carry a pad map — refused by name otherwise. Omitted from the wire when null.

solid.description: The screen slab's solidity facet (a box collider derived from the slab's oriented frame + Margin by Server.WorldColliderSet), or null for a decorative screen. Omitted from the wire when null.

magazine.description: The per-screen source magazine (the cycle primitive), or null for a screen with no magazine — nothing to cycle. Omitted from the wire when null — the whole-row UpsertScreen carries it for free, so no new mutation kind is needed.

entries.description: The ordered source list (at least one entry).

items.description: The signal carried by a WorldScreen's lit face. A source declares which provider feeds a slot; the engine resolves and samples it. The $type string is the JSON discriminator; a new source kind is a new derived record plus its JsonDerivedTypeAttribute line.

selected.description: The 0-based entry the selector starts on (what screen.select advances from), not what the screen boots showing — a screen always wakes on its declared Source (the one-live-console ceiling depends on this). Live selection drifts from this and is folded back by world.save (see Puck.World.WorldSessionCapture).

wrap.description: Whether advancing past the last entry returns to the first (the arcade cabinet's wrapping cycle); when false the selector clamps at both ends.

memory.description: The screen's live byte-window bindings between its booted machine's bus and ordinary state.world Int cells (see WorldScreenMemory), or null for a screen with none. Omitted from the wire when null.

items.description: One live byte-window binding between a declared screens row's booted machine and an ordinary state.world Int cell — the campfire seam: a 3D log on the fire is a cell, the cartridge reads it (or, the other direction, a lever the cartridge throws is a cell the 3D world reads). A Direction of Read mirrors the machine's bytes into the cell every tick through the ordinary state-mutation door (WorldMutation.UpsertStateCell, the same door a rule's own single-cell write folds into — see Server.WorldServer.MachineMemory.cs), a write landing only when the peeked value changed, so a quiet machine costs nothing; Write pokes the cell's current value into the machine's bus (PokeByte through Server.IWorldMachineHost.TryPokeMessage) every tick the cell's value has moved since the last poke — a mutation of the machine's guest state through the host seam, deterministic under replay because the value it carries is itself simulation state a replay reproduces bit-for-bit, unlike a bare debug poke's own unrecorded-input caveat. Distinct from an addon row's own WorldAddonMemoryWatch (an edge-triggered event feed for a mounted guest): this binding is a standing per-tick mirror into ordinary state, read by every other state consumer (rules, HUD bindings, a placement's respond) with no addon in the loop.

address.description: The machine bus address the window starts at. Validated within 0..(MaxAddress - Width + 1) — outside the engine's addressable memory refuses by name at validation, never at runtime (a machine's own IMachineMemoryPeek silently reads/no-ops out of its own smaller readable/writable range instead, exactly as it does for any other peek/poke).

width.description: How many bytes the window spans, little-endian (the low byte at Address): 1 or 2.

row.description: The declared state.world row this binding mirrors to/from — must resolve to a kind=Int row.

key.description: The cell inside Row, or null for its slot cell. Refused when Row is keyed and this is absent, or unkeyed and this is present — the same (row, key) pair rule every other named-cell reference in this document follows. Omitted from the wire when null.

direction.description: Which way the binding moves a value.
